hypothesis: A release that leaves the resources' shared compose project never retires its app container there: apply_on_host retires only the projects it was told to (retire_own_projects, which rightly refuses a project that also holds the resource service and its data), so the earlier release's app container keeps holding the published port and compose up fails with 'port is already allocated'.
why_not_the_recommendation: The recommendation proposed fixing the single-container retire step and widening own_projects. The single-container step only knows the one-container release, and widening own_projects would let a clean take the shared project down with the resource service and its data. The missing piece is a retire of only this app's own containers inside the shared project an earlier release ran in.
test_plan: Drive apply_on_host for a release that runs as its own project while an earlier release of the same target ran in the shared project; the steps sent to the host must remove exactly the app's own container there (by compose working_dir), before compose up, never the resource service, another app's container or a volume.
